identity_evidence: Text says 'November 25, 1927' and '[No. 4767]', Coolidge, designating Judge James W. Blackburn Special Judge of the Canal Zone.
outliers_found: one-person appointment (spent on issue; belongs elsewhere)
basis: The order designates one named person as special judge of the Canal Zone, which the lot card lists as an outlier. It also ends by its own terms on January 1, 1929, but the lot does not accept one-person appointments.
operative_quote:
I designate Judge James W. Blackburn as Special Judge of
the Canal Zone until January 1, 1929
notes: OCR is rough at the top and bottom but the body is clear. Own term ends 1929-01-01.

identity_evidence: Wikisource page 'Executive Order 3347 (1920)', signed Saturday October 30, 1920, 'Licensing of Chauffeurs in the Canal Zone'.
basis: The order widens the word 'automobile' in the Canal Zone chauffeur-licensing order of October 9, 1918 to cover all motor-propelled vehicles and motorcycles; it governs only licensing within the Canal Zone, so it had no object after the Zone and the U.S. canal operation ended.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote: shall be construed to include any and all motor-propelled vehicles, and shall specifically include motorcycles.
notes: Wikisource page scrape; boilerplate around the order text.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 2014 (1914)', signed Thursday, August 6, 1914, 'To Reorganize the Board of Health of The Canal Zone'.
basis: The order sets up the Canal Zone Board of Health, its membership and its power to make sanitary rules for the Zone, and repeals four sections of an Isthmian Canal Commission act; all of it is Zone government with no reach outside the Zone.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote: There is hereby established a Board of Health, under the jurisdiction of the Health Department, consisting of the following officials heretofore appointed by the Governor:
notes: The repeal of sections 13-16 of Act 8 is a Zone-government matter and is treated as the same kind of command. Zone government itself ended 1979-10-01.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 1319 (1911)', signed March 16, 1911, 'Appointing Walter W. Warwick Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the Canal Zone'.
outliers_found: one-person appointment (spent on issue; belongs elsewhere)
basis: The order's only command is the appointment of one named person as associate justice of the Canal Zone Supreme Court, an outlier on the lot card.
operative_quote:
Walter W. Warwick is appointed an Associate Justice of the Supreme 
Court of the Canal Zone, at a salary of six thousand dollars per annum

identity_evidence: Text contains '[No. 6997]' after the alcoholic-beverages-in-the-Canal-Zone order, dated 'March 26, 1935'; claimed number 6997 agrees.
basis: The order sets licensing, sale, importation and manufacture rules for alcoholic beverages in the Canal Zone under the Act of June 19, 1934; it operates only within the Zone.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote:
From and after the date of this order it shall be unlawful in the Canal Zone
to sell or import any alcoholic beverage except as provided herein.
notes: The text file begins with a different order (No. 6996-A, an NRA agreement approval dated March 22, 1935), which was ignored. The text of 6997 is dated March 26, 1935, while the claimed date is 1935-03-25: a one-day date conflict, with the number agreeing.

identity_evidence: The visible text has no order number and no date; only the subject (highways, vehicles and traffic regulations in the Canal Zone) and the reference to the Canal Zone Code approved June 19, 1934 agree with the claim.
basis: The text is cut off after about 12,000 of 57,815 characters, before any date, signature or order number, so it cannot be tied to Executive Order 7242 of December 6, 1935 on its own words. The visible portion is Zone-only traffic regulation.
operative_quote: Section 11. Governor authorized to make regulations. The Governor is hereby authorized to make, alter, and amend, from time to time, rules and regulations for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this Order.
notes: Truncated by the packet (marker: original 57815 characters). Article 8 (revocation of prior orders; effective date) was not visible and could not be checked.

identity_evidence: The text is Wikisource 'Executive Order 1917 (1914)' signed April 16, 1914, on payment of tolls and bills for services to vessels by the Panama Canal, not EO 665 of 1907-08-15 on reorganizing the Washington office of the commission.
basis: The text is a different order (No. 1917, 1914), so identity fails.
notes: Claimed EO 665 (Aug 15, 1907). The text matches neither the number nor the date nor the subject.

identity_evidence: Text dated 'September 19, 1914', amending paragraph E of section 12 of the Executive Order of March 20, 1914 on injury compensation for Panama Canal and Panama Railroad Company employees; matches claimed title and date.
basis: The order replaces one paragraph on compensation for dependents of employees of the Panama Canal and Panama Railroad Company who die of injury, effective April 1, 1914; payments are at the Governor's discretion and capped at eight years, so no payment can still run.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended); payments capped at eight years per beneficiary
operative_quote: there may be paid to such relation monthly such portion or portions of the monthly pay of the employee as may be determined by the Governor of The Panama Canal
notes: The text carries no order number; identity rests on date and subject. The order is employee compensation (conditions of service in the Zone). I found no sign of a continuing individual right in the text, but a second reviewer may want to check whether a later statute preserved such claims.

identity_evidence: Text ends '13 October, 1914. [ No. 2062.]' on license taxes and fees for the Canal Zone.
basis: The order sets license taxes and fees for vehicles, dances, peddlers and similar businesses in the Canal Zone, collected through the Zone's Executive Secretary and Collector; it operates only in the Zone.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote:
There shall be collected the following taxes for operating, in the streets
and roads of the Canal Zone, public vehicles
notes: OCR noise in a few words; scanned page text. Zone government ended 1979-10-01.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 1386 (1911)', signed Friday, July 21, 1911, 'Providing for the Inspection of Steam Vessels' in the Canal Zone.
basis: The order sets annual inspection, certificates, fees and fines for steam vessels navigating Canal Zone waters, run by the Zone's Board of Local Inspectors; it operates only in the Zone.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote: All steam vessels navigating the waters of the Canal Zone, except public vessels of the United States or other countries, shall be subject to the provisions of this Order.
notes: Truncated after section 20 (original 14,777 characters); the unseen end is probably the appeal procedure and effective date.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 1412 (1911)', signed Thursday, September 14, 1911; claimed date '1911' and title agree.
basis: The order makes removing packing or waste from journal boxes of railroad equipment a misdemeanor, as an order for the Canal Zone; it applies only in the Zone.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote: By virtue of the authority vested in me I hereby establish the following Order for the Canal Zone.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 1990 (1914)', signed Thursday, July 9, 1914, rules and regulations for the operation and navigation of the Panama Canal.
basis: The order sets navigation, pilotage and transit rules for vessels using the Panama Canal and its waters, enforced by the U.S. canal authorities; these functions ended when the canal passed to Panama.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote: Any person violating any of the provisions of the rules and regulations established hereunder shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor
notes: Truncated: only about 12,000 of 73,628 characters were visible, so later rules were not checked for other kinds of command.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 335-A (1905)', signed June 24, 1905, designating a Board of Consulting Engineers; date and subject agree with the claim (the number carries suffix -A).
outliers_found: named appointments of several persons (spent on issue)
content reaches outside the Zone and the canal's operation (board meets in Washington, includes foreign engineers, decides on plans)
basis: The order appoints a board of named engineers to meet in Washington and consider plans for building the canal; it does not govern the Zone or the canal's operation, and it is a set of appointments.
operative_quote: shall convene in the city of Washington, at the rooms of the Isthmian Canal Commission, on the first day of September, nineteen hundred and five
notes: The order is numbered 335-A on the page; the claim says 335.

identity_evidence: Text dated 'June 11, 1909', signed Wm. H. Taft, amending paragraph 6 of the Executive Order of January 6, 1909 about old French dump cars on the Panama Canal; date and subject agree with the claimed title.
basis: The order only changes the effective date of the earlier safety-appliance order for railroad equipment on the Panama Canal, with an exception ending July 1, 1910; it concerns only equipment of the canal works.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended); the exception ran to 1910-07-01 on its own terms
operative_quote: except for the use of old French dump cars in use on the Panama Canal, including also the couplers of locomotives necessary to operate them, until July 1, 1910
notes: The text has no order number and never says 'Canal Zone' or 'safety appliances'; identity rests on the date and the Panama Canal equipment. A second reviewer should check the claim that this is EO 1085.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 664 (1907)', signed August 15, 1907, reorganizing accounting and disbursing offices of the Isthmian Canal Commission; matches claimed number, date and subject.
basis: The order reorganizes the Commission's accounting and disbursing offices on the Isthmus and in Washington, including audit of the Canal Zone Government's accounts; the offices belonged to the U.S. canal work and the Commission itself was later replaced.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote: That on and after August 15, 1907, the positions of General Auditor and Local Auditor be abolished.
notes: Some duties are performed in Washington (Assistant Examiner, Disbursing Officer in the United States) for the Commission's canal accounts; I treated these as part of the canal operation, but a second reviewer may see this as reaching outside the Zone.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 2026 (1914)', signed Saturday, August 22, 1914, 'Regulating Operation of Street Railway Cars at Crossings', for the Canal Zone.
basis: The order sets speed, signal and stop rules for street railway cars at crossings in the Canal Zone with a fine or jail penalty; it operates only there.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote: It shall be unlawful for a motorman or any person in control of a street railway car to run same over or upon any street crossing

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 348-C (1905)', signed August 31, 1905, compensation for members of the Advisory Board of Engineers for the Panama Canal; date and subject agree with the claim (the number carries suffix -C).
outliers_found: named persons given extra pay (Gen. Davis and Gen. Abbott)
content is about a consulting board on canal plans, not Zone government or the canal's operation
basis: The order pays each member of the consulting board $5,000 plus expenses and increases the pay of two named generals; it is a one-time payment order on a planning board, not a rule about the Zone or the canal's operation, so it does not fit the lot.
operative_quote: each member of the advisory board of engineers upon plans of the Panama Canal shall be allowed $5,000, payable upon the completion of the report of the board.
notes: The order is numbered 348-C on the page; the claim says 348.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 2204 (1915)', signed Tuesday, May 25, 1915, modifying the Executive Order of January 15, 1915 on rent, fuel and electric current for employees of the Panama Canal and Panama Railroad Company; the claim names E.O. 2120 of Jan. 15, 1915.
basis: The order suspends charges for rent, fuel and lights for canal employees on the Isthmus during actual construction but not later than June 30, 1916; it is a condition of service that ended by its own terms.
operative_quote: is modified by suspending from the operation thereof so much as relates to rent, fuel, and lights during the period of actual construction of the Panama Canal but not later than June 30, 1916.
notes: Claimed title is truncated ('amended t...'); the text agrees on date and subject.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 3031 (1919)', signed Saturday, January 25, 1919, leave for Canal Zone employees returning from military or naval service.
basis: The order credits leave to Panama Canal and Panama Railroad Company employees who left to enter wartime service and return to duty within 90 or 120 days; it is a condition of service of canal employees in the Zone and any return window closed long ago.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Treaty terminated; U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote: shall, upon return to duty with The Panama Canal or Panama Railroad Company within the periods designated, be credited with leave at the rate of 1/12th of the year's allowance of leave
notes: Employees' conditions of service are within the lot; I saw no continuing individual right that a later statute preserved.
